target.title: feat(nodes): add computer use (computer.act) on macOS nodes via Peekaboo
target.body:
Related: #97333

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw agents could see a desktop node's screen (`screen.snapshot`) but could not act on it — there was no way for an agent to click, type, scroll, or drag on a paired macOS machine. This adds agent-driven desktop control, so a Mac node can be driven end-to-end (screenshot → reason → act) instead of being a read-only surface.

## Why This Change Was Made

The contract is deliberately **node-agnostic**: the agent emits one dangerous node command, `computer.act`, whose action set mirrors Anthropic's `computer_20251124` (click/type/key/scroll/drag/zoom/wait, modifiers on the `text` field). The agent cannot tell how a node fulfills it. macOS nodes fulfill it **in-process** via the Peekaboo automation engine already embedded in OpenClaw.app, so mouse/keyboard synthesis runs under the signed app's Accessibility + Screen-Recording grants (no ambient-binary TCC widening). Other platforms can later fulfill the identical `computer.act` — e.g. via an MCP — with zero agent-side change.

Safety is built in:
- **Dangerous-by-default.** `computer.act` is on the dangerous-command list and is excluded from the runtime allowlist until explicitly armed; the pairing surface still advertises it so the node can be armed. Arming reuses phone-control's `operator.admin`-gated, time-bounded `arm`/`disarm` (new `computer` group).
- **Screenshots are model-only.** Coordinate-bearing screenshots go to the model and are never auto-delivered to chat channels (#44759).
- **Coordinate frame is bound and validated.** Coordinates map against the exact `{node, display, delivered-pixel-width}` the model observed; input actions fail closed when no matching screenshot frame exists, reject out-of-frame/partial/`refWidth<=0` coordinates, clamp to the selected display, and serialize per tool instance so parallel tool calls can't reorder real desktop input.

## User Impact

An operator can enable Computer Control on a Mac node and arm it (`/phone arm computer --for 30m`); the agent can then screenshot the desktop and click, type, use key combos, scroll, and drag. It is off by default, requires the OpenClaw.app Accessibility/Screen-Recording grants, and is time-boxed. No behavior changes for anyone who does not enable it.

## Evidence

**Local proof (all green):**
- TS: `computer-tool` tool tests (contract, coordinate scaling, frame binding, fail-closed, node-switch, multi-display), plus `node-command-policy` (dangerous-by-default, pairing-under-denylist regression), `node-connect-reconcile`, and `phone-control` arming.
- Swift: OpenClawKit `ComputerInputGeometry` unit tests (Retina/portrait/landscape scaling, display clamp, non-positive refWidth); `OpenClaw` app target compiles against Peekaboo 3.5.2; Mac node runtime tests (`computer.act` routing, disabled-gate, cap advertisement).
- Rebased onto latest `main` and re-verified: TS suites, OpenClawKit tests, full app build, and 56 Mac-node Swift tests pass.

**Review:** Codex autoreview run to convergence over six rounds; 13 findings fixed (coordinate scaling, drag-modifier retention, watchdog refresh, fresh-setup denylist pairing bug, multi-display targeting, delivered-dimension reporting, frame binding, out-of-frame/partial/`refWidth` validation, and per-instance serialization for parallel tool calls).

**Outstanding before merge (this is why the PR is a draft):**
1. **Signed clawmac live run** — a real agent computer-use task on the device (signed build + Accessibility/Screen-Recording granted) has not yet been executed. This is the primary pre-merge gate.
2. **Button-hold lifecycle cleanup (follow-up).** After `left_mouse_down`, if arm expiry / `/phone disarm` / disconnect / disabling Computer Control prevents the matching `left_mouse_up`, only a 120s idle watchdog releases the synthetic button. A lifecycle-release hook (release outstanding input on disable/disconnect/disarm) should replace the watchdog as the primary cleanup.
